Q: Validate file content from malicious script A:

The security team has asked me to validate the Prompt field. If it contains elements such as <script>, <!-->, or similar patterns, the file should be rejected to prevent SQL injection or malicious scripts

None of this makes much sense.

SQL injection isn't caused by any of the examples you noted, nor is it caused per se by what people type into a prompt field or save in a file. SQL injection is caused by using input data (from any source) in a string that is then passed to the SQL database to execute, without correctly parameterising it. That's something you fix by writing your code properly, not by trying to control the contents of an input field - you cannot possibly hope to remove all SQL injection threats by such a method in any case.

By "malicious scripts" it seems (from your examples) you are probably talking about XSS injection into a web page. Again this is not solved by input filtering. Think about it - if you strip or encode characters from the input data before you store it in your application, then that stored data becomes useful in only one context - a HTML document - because it will be distorted in any other environment - e.g. an entirely legitimate < character in the input would be come < if you HTML-encode it at that time. Real-world applications output data to all sorts of contexts (maybe a spreadsheet or a PDF would be common examples) and so you would be outputting messed-up data if you store it already XSS-proof. Instead, you must mitigate the XSS threat in context. In other words, you must HTML-encode this data at the time you are about to output it into a HTML document - because that's the only time at which the data is potentially problematic in terms of XSS. The data can't hurt you while it's sitting in your database, or in Excel, or in a PDF, because they don't execute scripts in the same way.

So... as we can see, it seems unfortunately that neither you or your "security team" have much understanding of the threats you're trying to mitigate, and nor does it appear that you've made any real attempt to research them, aside from asking this rather misguided question. Yet the correct mitigations for these threats are well-known and well-documented online already in many places, both in general terms and with specifics for the programming language(s) and environment(s) you happen to be working with. As I've already indicated none of those techniques have anything to do with the filtering approach you have asked about. As such your post is a classic X-Y Problem.

A good place to start understing this topic properly is the OWASP top 10 web application security threats, which is updated annually.

We usually use a simple Regex check to filter out special characters

What do you consider to be a "special" character, and why? In reality there is no such thing.

Again if we take the examples you provided, we might assume you are concerned about things like < and > and ! and -. But why are they special? They're entirely normal characters and could appear in many different types of text, for entirely legitimate reasons. They are not, by themselves, dangerous. Even whole chunks of text such as <script> are not, by themselves, dangerous. They're just text, at this point in your process. It's what you do with them later which could introduce problems. But it does very much depend what you do with them as to whether they become a problem. Again: context is everything. As I alluded to above when discussing XSS, removing or encoding them at input time is completely counterproductive and will just corrupt acceptable data unnecessarily.

Q: RSA Encryption and Decryption with X509certificate2 A:

This is not the exact answer which you might expected but I write here as it's too long as a comment.

I think the decryption itself has no problem at all (I've found the example blog of your code with php encryption) That's why I commented I was curious on the encryptedstring which is the target of decryption.

I also struggled in understanding Security for months and now I use symmetric(AES) and asymmetric(RSA) together. Understanding is really important and everybody takes time..

RSA is asymmetric and one-way which means the Encryption can be done only by public key and the Decryption can be done only by private key. You're using private key in Encryption method and it seems just copied from Decryption.

The answer by Zesty is right only in terms of formatting. You're also needed to understand the formatting. We need Convert.ToBase64String and Convert.FromBase64String in Encryption and Decryption from byte to base64string and vice versa. However this base64string is not just plain like 'hello' but 'SABlAGwAbABvACAAVwBvAHIAbABkAA==' as you see here

And I kindly recommend to use complete solution(not half one like php encryption) like this blog so that Encryption and Decryption and all are in harmony.

And as last as I commented also, you're needed to think about how to prevent the black users if encryption is done from client side and you don't have only good users.

I hope my experience helps to understand Security which is of most importance.

Q: centos+enabling mbstring extension in php.ini still not showing in phpinfo() A:
  1. First install mbstring
sudo yum install php-mbstring

  1. check if the mbstring is appearing in php -m | grep mbstring

  2. check the extension directory in phpinfo in my case it was /usr/lib64/php/modules/

  3. httpd/appache is looking for extensions in /etc/httpd/modules
    In my case, I copied the file

$ cp /usr/lib64/php/modules/mbstring.so /etc/httpd/modules/mbstring.so
  1. sudo service httpd restart

Note then if you are using AWS EC2 try to stop and start the server to reload the new modules it works for me just after stopping and starting EC2

  1. [optional] last in php.ini put
[mbstring]
mbstring.language = all
mbstring.internal_encoding = UTF-8
mbstring.http_input = auto
mbstring.http_output = UTF-8
mbstring.encoding_translation = On
mbstring.detect_order = UTF-8
mbstring.substitute_character = none;
mbstring.func_overload = 0
mbstring.strict_encoding = Off

Q: Android Error: Binary XML file line #11: Error inflating class fragment when using map fragment A:

From your error log: Binary XML file line #11: Must specify unique android:id, android:tag, or have a parent with an id for com.google.android.gms.maps.MapFragment

From the official documentation:

https://developer.android.com/guide/components/fragments.html

You should specify ID and TAG for your fragment.

So change your layout from :

<fragment 
    class="com.google.android.gms.maps.MapFragment"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent" />
</RelativeLayout>

to:

<fragment 
    android:id="@+id/your_desired_id"
    android:tag="tag"
    class="com.google.android.gms.maps.MapFragment"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="match_parent" />
</RelativeLayout>
